- **[important]** `src/skills/the-algorithm/references/algorithm.md:219` — **Remove revived dead reference**
  The new doctrine says, "Full schema and presets: `PAI/ALGORITHM/parameter-schema.md`", but this PR removes `parameter-schema.md` as absent. An executor following the ideate/optimize path reaches a nonexistent dependency.

- **[blocker]** `src/skills/the-algorithm/references/algorithm.md:38` — **Removed capability contract remains claimed**
  The added doctrine says "The thinking-capability vocabulary is a CLOSED ENUMERATION" and names `capabilities.md` as its authority, while the PR removes that missing file and states the CLI accepts a free string. Its later claim that a "Capability-Name Audit Gate" rejects omissions therefore misleads users into believing an enforcement mechanism exists.

## Confirmed on the real environment

- **[important]** `CONTEXT.md:689` — **Glossary asserts runtime enforcement the spec says is bypassable**
  The glossary entry — the text projected into every session — says the autonomy class is one "that the runtime enforces at close time", with no qualifier, while `docs/work-graph.md:128` admits "Bypass via raw `gh` remains visible-but-unprevented in phase 1" and the detecting auditor is phase 2, gated on a machine account that does not exist. An agent reading the glossary will treat a closed node as gate-passed when nothing checked it.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:87` — **Frontier releases dependents on unverified closes; unmentioned**
  "**Frontier** = open ∧ unassigned ∧ all blockers closed" derives release purely from tracker status, while the same change concedes raw tracker writes are "visible-but-unprevented" — so one hand-closed issue silently makes every dependent node claimable without any checkpoint gate ever running. The spec names the bypass but never this propagation path, and it fails open.

- **[suggestion]** `src/cli/policy.ts:283` — **`soma policy probes` accepts two competing home overrides**
  The parser takes both `--home-dir` and `--soma-home` and passes both through to `loadProbeRegistry`, but the documented override surface is one flag: "Concretely `~/.soma/policy/probe-registry.json` (override with `soma graph close --soma-home`)". Two overrides on an authorisation-list reader make it ambiguous which path an adopter is actually inspecting.
  Fix: Document the precedence of `--home-dir` vs `--soma-home` in §2.2, or drop `--home-dir` from `policy probes` to match the single documented override.

- **[suggestion]** `src/cli/policy.ts:289` — **Inspection verb can read a registry the gate never consults**
  Spec: "`soma policy probes [--repo <owner/name>]` shows what is declared and where" — the documented signature carries no home override, yet the parser adds `--soma-home` and `--home-dir` cases. An adopter verifying a declaration via a pointed home sees a registry the close path (which "takes no flag that moves it") will never read.
  Fix: Drop `--soma-home`/`--home-dir` from `POLICY_PROBES_USAGE` and the parser, or have the output name the resolved registry path so an override is visible in what it prints.

- **[suggestion]** `(PR description):0` — **Verification block describes the branch two commits ago**
  The description states "Diff is 6311 insertions / 10 deletions" and "`bun test` — 2208 pass / 0 fail", but `git diff --shortstat main...HEAD` reports 6458 insertions and the head commit's own message reports 2212 pass — the evidence predates the two commits that changed the close gate (`--evidence` refusal, `--soma-home` removal).

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:452` — **parseLabels treats null as absent but rejects other non-arrays**
  `if (value === undefined || value === null) return [];` silently accepts `labels: null` while `labels: "grilling"` throws `invalid-node`. A caller sending JSON with an explicit null gets no signal that the field was ignored.
  Fix: Drop the `|| value === null` branch so null falls through to the array check, or document why null is treated as absent.

- **[important]** `src/skills/orienteer/references/closing.md:96` — **Approval gate accepts proposer self-ratification**
  The diff documents that ratification falls back to the proposer: "on a single-credential deployment — where the agent posts the proposal *as* the principal — the principal's own 👍 ratifies too", and "Only the `attestation` label records that it was not the right human". An agent holding one credential can post a proposal, react to it, and close an `approve` node with `approved` evidence — the human gate is bypassed with an audit trail but no enforcement.
  Fix: Make proposer-self-ratification opt-in (e.g. `close` refuses it unless `--allow-self-ratify` is passed), so single-credential deployments choose the weakening explicitly.

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:126` — **Seam degrades silently per backend, with no declaration**
  The JSDoc states "A backend with no index concept ignores them", so an identical `--label` call is honoured on GitHub and dropped elsewhere with nothing distinguishing the two at the seam. CONTEXT.md's `policy enforcement level` entry sets the opposite pattern for the same problem — unavailable capability is declared by the adapter rather than silently pretended.
  Fix: Have `GraphStore` declare index support (e.g. a `capabilities.labels` flag) so a caller can tell written from dropped.

- **[blocker]** `src/cli/graph.ts:688` — **Self-👍 mints machine-trusted `approved` evidence, bypassing the --evidence control**
  The PR states it "does not touch the `--evidence` boundary check, which still refuses a hand-written `approved` entry" — but `return { kind: "reaction", id: selfApproval.id, author: selfApproval.author }` lets the same caller obtain that entry legitimately, and the test pins it: `expect(store.closed[0].receipt.evidence.some((entry) => entry.kind === "approved")).toBe(true)`. A consumer that keys on `evidence.kind === "approved"` — the reason hand-writing it is refused — can no longer distinguish a second-party approval from a self-approval; only the separate `attestation` field carries that, and §3.2 says it is a label, not a gate.
  Fix: Emit a distinct evidence kind (e.g. `self-approved`) on the fallback path so the trust level is visible where consumers actually read it, not only in `attestation`.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:346` — **Sole remaining safeguard is held by the credential it must restrain**
  The new doc leans on "A 👎 from the root node's author suppresses ratification outright" as the safeguard, while the same paragraph concedes "the agent posts proposals *as* the principal, so every 👍 available is a self-ratification" — on that deployment the vetoing account, the proposing account, and the ratifying account are one token. A leaked PAT or an injected agent session can therefore propose, react, and close every `approve`-class HITL node unattended, with the only trace a receipt field that gates nothing.
  Fix: Require an explicit opt-in (config or `--allow-self-ratification`) for the fallback so the reduced control is a deployment decision, not the default close path.

- **[important]** `src/cli/graph.ts:686` — **Close-time policy lives in the CLI, not the graph module**
  `selectRatification` now carries a 12-line doctrine comment citing "§3.2 is explicit that attestation is a label" and implements three-tier ratifier precedence, yet it sits in `src/cli/graph.ts` while the spec it enforces is `docs/work-graph.md` and the type layer is `src/work-graph.ts`. Any non-CLI consumer of the graph (daemon, MCP surface, another substrate) reimplements or bypasses this policy.
  Fix: Move `selectRatification` next to `deriveAttestation`/`parseNodeSpec` in `src/work-graph.ts`; re-export from the CLI.

- **[suggestion]** `src/skills/orienteer/Workflows/ChartTheMap.md:46` — **GitHub label semantics baked into backend-neutral skill doctrine**
  "On GitHub an unknown label is created by the call rather than rejected by it, so there is no pre-step" states one backend's behaviour as workflow doctrine, while `CreateNodeSpec` is explicitly the backend-agnostic seam where "a backend with no index concept ignores them". A second `GraphStore` that rejects unknown labels makes this instruction wrong without any code change.
  Fix: Qualify as "on the GitHub store" and note that label acceptance is backend-defined.

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:458` — **Creation-only label validation also runs on the read path**
  `parseNodeSpec` is reused by `nodeFromIssue` to parse the issue-body block, so `const labels = parseLabels(record.labels)` now validates a key that can only get there by hand-editing the tracker; a block containing `"labels": 5` throws `"labels" must be an array of strings` and downgrades an otherwise-valid node to `untypedNode` (autonomy `approve`), where before the key was silently ignored. Labels are a creation input that legitimately never appears in a block.
  Fix: Ignore `record.labels` when parsing a stored block, or drop the key before the round-trip in `nodeFromIssue`.

- **[important]** `src/skills/orienteer/references/map.md:85` — **Label-based map discovery trusts an attacker-writable attribute**
  Doctrine changes map discovery from "Find it by id" to "Find it by id, or by its `orienteer:map` label", and `gh issue list --label orienteer:map` "finds every map in a repo". A GitHub triage-role account (label rights, no push) can attach `orienteer:map` to any issue; a later orienteer session discovers it and reads its Notes — which the workflow defines as "standing preferences, and any override of the plan-don't-do default" — as directives. Label-write rights become agent-instruction authority.
  Fix: Keep id (or the typed node block) as the authoritative discovery path; document label-based listing as a browsing aid whose results must be confirmed against the node block before their Notes are acted on.

- **[important]** `test/work-graph-github.test.ts:207` — **Node-block expectation computed from the spec it is meant to check**
  The expectation `body: \`## Question

which?

${encodeNodeBlock(spec)}\`` derives the persisted block from the same labelled `spec`, so if `encodeNodeBlock` serializes `labels` into the block the test still passes — and `readNode` would then read them back, breaking the PR's load-bearing claim that labels "are never read back" and "never become node state". The PR sells this test as pinning "the **whole** `POST /issues` body", but the only part that could carry the leak is asserted against itself.

- **[blocker]** `src/skills/orienteer/references/map.md:89` — **Claimed doc correction has no deletion in the diff**
  The description quotes shipped doctrine — "create the `orienteer:*` labels before the first `add` — the create call fails on a label that does not exist" — calls it "**Untested, and false**", and says "that is what the docs now say"; but map.md removes only the sentence "an `orienteer:map` label is optional human decoration…" (-2 lines) and ChartTheMap.md removes only "specified**. The body template is in `references/map.md`." (-1 line). The false instruction is deleted nowhere in this PR, so a reviewer is told a correction landed while the wrong guidance is still shipped wherever it actually lives.

- **[suggestion]** `src/skills/orienteer/references/map.md:84` — **Motivating evidence is an unlinked self-authored anecdote**
  "The tell was in this repo's own history — three nodes on map #495 got `wayfinder:grilling` applied by hand while walking it, compensating for something the same session had just removed" is the only empirical support offered for the new "**Always label a node you create**" doctrine, with no link and no way for a reader to check either the three nodes or the causal reading. The intent attributed to that session is inference stated as observed fact.

- **[important]** `src/work-graph.ts:650` — **Single-operator rationale, unconditional removal**
  The in-code justification is scoped — "on a single-operator deployment the ratification gate named none" — but `if (node.autonomy !== "auto") return;` drops the gate for every deployment, and the PR states two attempts to derive "single operator" failed. docs/work-graph.md names the counter-case ("a multi-party deployment") only to wave it off as "a label on the record, never a gate on the close", without engaging what enforces the gate there.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:338` — **Spec deletes the definition of `approved`, which is still live**
  The hunk removes "`approved` evidence is an attestation verifiable as coming from **a credential the agent does not hold**" and the #486 mechanics, but `approved` remains a receipt evidence kind (`ratification = selectRatification(...); if (ratification !== undefined) { evidence.push({`) and the "#### Deriving `attestation` (#502)" section directly below still derives from it. The canonical spec now names a term it no longer defines.
  Fix: Keep the `approved` definition paragraph under "What remains", qualified with "admissible, no longer required".

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:338` — **"One change" hides doctrine deleted from the canonical doc**
  The description asserts "One change: `assertClosable` no longer requires ratified evidence", but this hunk also deletes the #486 definition of `approved` evidence ("verifiable as coming from **a credential the agent does not hold** ... verified via the API author field") and the replay-rebind rule ("A materially amended proposal is re-posted and needs fresh ratification"), neither mentioned anywhere in the PR. A reviewer approving on "one change" never audits the removed normative rules, which still govern the proposal flow the PR says survives.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:373` — **Multi-party mitigation names a consumer the PR says does not exist**
  The doc justifies removing the gate for every deployment because "a reviewer or the phase-2 auditor can act on it after the fact", while the PR description states the phase-2 headless tick "does not exist, and may not". The change deletes a gate for naming no consumer, then defends the deletion by naming a consumer that is not there.

- **[blocker]** `src/work-graph.ts:649` — **Removal justified by receipt fields the default path never writes**
  The comment defending the unconditional removal claims "A multi-party deployment instead gets the receipt: proposal, ratifier, root authorship and confinement are all still recorded" (and repeats it at :653), yet docs/work-graph.md:388-390 in this same PR retracts exactly that sentence — "an earlier draft claimed the receipt carried 'proposal, ratifier, root authorship and confinement' ... On the default path the first two are absent." A consumer reading the seam gets the version the PR knows to be false, attached to the load-bearing argument for dropping the gate.

- **[important]** `src/cli/graph.ts:806` — **Veto throws before the dry-run branch**
  `if (vetoed) { throw new SomaCliError(...) }` runs before `if (parsed.options.dryRun === true)`, unlike the probe-refusal check just above it which is explicitly guarded by `parsed.options.dryRun !== true` ("A dry run keeps going: showing the whole receipt is the point of asking for one"). `soma graph close <id> --proposal-comment <id> --dry-run` now exits 1 and prints no receipt, even though a dry run writes nothing.
  Fix: Guard the veto the same way (`vetoed && parsed.options.dryRun !== true`) and surface the refusal in the preview verdict instead; add a test alongside "--dry-run still renders the receipt when the registry refused a probe".

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:630` — **24-line rationale comment guards a one-line return**
  The block from `// Evidence is required of \`auto\` nodes only` through `// It is a tool, no longer a toll.` is 24 lines of prose fronting `if (node.autonomy !== "auto") return;`, and its substance ("The removal is UNCONDITIONAL... two attempts to derive it failed review") is already the canonical text in docs/work-graph.md. Two full copies of a design argument drift apart on the next edit.
  Fix: Keep 2-3 lines at the guard ("HITL closes on the session's say-so; gate named no consumer — see docs/work-graph.md §3.2 and #499") and let the doc own the argument.

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:630` — **33-line comment guards a one-line return**
  The diff adds 33 lines of rationale (`// The removal is UNCONDITIONAL...`, `// The receipt still records everything it recorded before...`) in front of `if (node.autonomy !== "auto") return;`. A reader scrolls a screen of argument to reach one branch, and the argument will rot independently of the code.
  Fix: Keep two lines here ("HITL closes on the session's say-so — see docs/work-graph.md §3.2") and let the doc hold the argument.

- **[suggestion]** `src/cli/graph.ts:802` — **Veto counts the proposer's own 👎, unlike ratification**
  `reaction.content === "-1" && root?.author !== undefined && reaction.author === root.author` applies no proposer exclusion, while the line below passes `proposal.author` to `selectRatification` precisely so a self-👍 is ignored. When the operator posts the proposal under their own credential (what `close --propose` does), their own 👎 permanently refuses that comment id while their own 👍 counts for nothing.
  Fix: Either exclude `proposal.author` from the veto for symmetry, or note in the comment that self-refusal is intentionally honoured where self-ratification is not.

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:630` — **27-line rationale comment guards one-line return**
  The block from `// Evidence is required of \`auto\` nodes only` through `// It is a tool, no longer a toll.` precedes a single statement, `if (node.autonomy !== "auto") return;`. A reader scrolls a screen of PR-description prose to reach one line of logic, and the prose will drift from the code on the next change.
  Fix: Keep two lines here (`HITL closes on the session's say-so; removal is unconditional — see docs/work-graph.md §3.2`) and let the spec hold the argument.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:380` — **"Two attempts to derive it failed review (#532)" cites one issue for two events**
  The canonical spec attributes both derivation failures to a single reference — "two attempts to derive it failed review (#532)" — with no second citation, so a reader cannot check either attempt. The load-bearing justification for making the removal unconditional rests on evidence that is not locatable from the citation given.

- **[suggestion]** `docs/work-graph.md:355` — **"Available, not required" overstated: bare close silently skips refusal**
  The spec frames the proposal flow as optional convenience — "The proposal flow is available, not required" — while the CLI branch `state.node.autonomy !== "auto" && commentId !== undefined` means the documented default path (`soma graph close <id>`) is precisely the one where a recorded 👎 has zero effect. The framing sells opting out as neutral when it is the path that disables the only surviving check.

- **[suggestion]** `src/cli/graph.ts:787` — **`--proposal-comment` silently ignored on auto nodes**
  The guard `state.node.autonomy !== "auto" && commentId !== undefined` means an `auto` node passed `--proposal-comment <id>` never reads the comment, never records a proposal, and never reports that the flag was dropped. Previously the flag was only reachable on non-auto nodes, so the silent-drop path is new.
  Fix: Error on `--proposal-comment` supplied for an `auto` node rather than ignoring it.

- **[important]** `src/cli/graph.ts:795` — **Refusal path newly reaches auto nodes, untested**
  The block moved out from under `if (state.node.autonomy !== "auto") {` and is now keyed on `if (commentId !== undefined)`, so an `auto` node passed `--proposal-comment` reads reactions and can hard-fail on a root-author 👎 — previously the flag was ignored there. No test in the diff passes `--proposal-comment` to an auto node.
  Fix: Add a test closing an `auto` node with `--proposal-comment` carrying a root-author 👎, pinning whichever outcome is intended.

- **[suggestion]** `src/cli/graph.ts:807` — **Refusal message contradicts the exit it accompanies**
  `Nothing here can stop you closing anyway — this is a reminder, not a gate.` is printed by the one code path that did stop the close (SomaCliError, exit 1), and unlike the message it replaces it names no next step.
  Fix: Say the close was refused and how to proceed, e.g. "re-propose with --propose and close on the new comment".

- **[suggestion]** `src/work-graph.ts:630` — **33-line rationale comment guards a one-line return**
  The block from "Evidence is required of `auto` nodes only" through "It is a tool, no longer a toll." precedes `if (node.autonomy !== "auto") return;` — six paragraphs of history, PR argument, and consumer analysis for one guard. A reader scrolls past a page of prose to reach two lines of logic.
  Fix: Keep 2-3 lines at the guard ("HITL closes on the session's say-so; removal is unconditional — see §3.2") and move the history/consumer argument to docs/work-graph.md, which already carries it.

- **[important]** `src/cli/graph.ts:806` — **Refusal check fails open when root author is unresolved**
  `reaction.author === root.author` is guarded by `root?.author !== undefined`, so when the root walk yields no author the predicate is uniformly false and every 👎 is silently ignored — the close proceeds with no signal that the refusal check did not run. `closing.md` documents this ("Where the root walk fails, no reaction matches and nothing refuses, silently") but the code emits nothing.
  Fix: When `root?.author === undefined` and reactions contain a `-1`, warn on stderr that the refusal check could not be evaluated.

- **[important]** `src/cli/graph.ts:788` — **Autonomy class drops out of the core seam into the CLI**
  The diff removes the `state.node.autonomy !== "auto"` branch from `runClose` and keys entirely on `commentId !== undefined`, with the comment conceding "`assertClosable` no longer distinguishes `propose` from `approve` from anything else non-`auto`". CONTEXT.md's work-graph entry states the node's autonomy class is a property "the spec obligates the runtime to enforce … at close time"; after this change no layer enforces a `propose`/`approve` distinction, so the glossary's three-class model has no runtime referent.
  Fix: Either collapse `propose`/`approve` into one class in the type and spec, or state in CONTEXT.md's work-graph entry that autonomy is now advisory metadata at close time.

- **[blocker]** `docs/work-graph.md:380` — **Cited #548 comment argues against the change it is cited to support**
  The spec's multi-party justification ends "with the reasoning in the closing comment of [#548]" — that comment actually says "The #499 deadlock was never evidence that solo deployments need a weaker gate; it was evidence that #511 is load-bearing" and closes with "Superseded by #511." A reader following the canonical citation finds a rejection of the removal, not its rationale.

- **[important]** `src/work-graph.ts:640` — **"Nobody else could ratify" contradicted by #496's existing credential split**
  The core comment justifies the unconditional removal with "where one person walks a map the ratification gate named none — nobody else could ratify"; #511's body records that #496 already achieved "authorship separation — proposal by `ivy-agent`, ratification by `jcfischer`, both API-attested" on this deployment. The alternative (finish the credential split) is never engaged anywhere in the diff or description.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:384` — **Cited commit does not contain the attempt it is cited for**
  The spec promises the failed derivations are "cited where they actually live: **graph-root authorship** ... and **one reachable credential** ..., both on branch `feat/self-ratification` at `b8acfe4`" — but `b8acfe4` is the commit that *deleted* graph-root authorship (`- if (rootAuthor === undefined || proposalAuthor !== rootAuthor) return undefined;` → `+ if (!sessionIsSingleCredential) return undefined;`); that attempt lives at `4950dae`, and the first credential-count attempt at `8cdab3a`. A reader auditing whether "not derivable" is earned lands on the removal, not the attempt.

- **[nit]** `test/cli-graph.test.ts:534` — **Eight-line test preamble duplicates the doc rationale again**
  The comment block ("#525 was going to add a rule; #549 removed the gate it would have served…") is a fourth copy of the same withdrawal story already in `work-graph.ts`, `work-graph.md`, and `closing.md`. Test comments should say what the test pins, not re-litigate the decision.
  Fix: Keep the first two lines (the amendment rule + why it holds structurally); drop the #525/#549 history.

- **[nit]** `src/cli/algorithm.ts:485` — **Guard comment claims parity with a differently-shaped arm**
  The comment says the new flags are "Scoped to `step`, matching the `--status` arm below" and complains about "two conventions in one switch", but `--status` does not refuse other actions — it dispatches (`if (action === "step") ... else` for criterion status). The cited parity does not exist, so the comment defends a third convention while claiming to remove ambiguity.

- **[important]** `src/algorithm.ts:640` — **setAlgorithmPlan un-bridge refusal is bypassable in two calls**
  The outgoing check compares against `run.planSteps`, so a caller drops the bridged step in one `setAlgorithmPlan` call ("Dropping the step from the plan entirely stays legal") and re-adds the same id unbridged in a second — the id survives with its authority removed, exactly what the refusal claims to prevent. The error message's own remedy ("Drop the step from the plan to remove it") is the first half of the bypass.
  Fix: Either accept the bypass explicitly in the docs/error text, or track dropped bridged ids on the run so re-adding one is refused.

**Blocker — `setAlgorithmPlan` silently un-bridges.** Correct: last round's guard was half a guard, inspecting only incoming steps. Both directions refuse now. Dropping the step from the plan entirely stays legal and is tested as such — the step ceases to exist, so nothing claims a node backs it; what is refused is the same id surviving with its authority quietly removed.

**Mutation evidence unsubstantiated** — fixed, and the criticism is right about what mattered. The mutations were genuinely run and the numbers are real, but nothing in the repo let a reader re-run them, so it read as a verified merge signal backed by nothing checkable. The three mutations and their expected failures are now recorded at the tests they justify, explicitly as a reproduction recipe rather than a standing gate, and the PR body no longer says "confirmed falsifiable". Worth noting mutation 3 is why the cycle test asserts at all — a `seen` set over a shape GitHub guarantees to be a tree reads like dead code until you remove it.

- **[suggestion]** `src/algorithm-capabilities.ts:580` — **Remove duplicate empty-registry guard**
  `if (definitions.length === 0 && unsupported.length === 0) { return run; }` appears at both lines 556 and 580, so the second branch is unreachable. Keeping both obscures the replacement policy and invites future edits to diverge.
  Fix: Keep the first guard and delete the second copy.

- **[important]** `test/bundled-skill-references.test.ts:143` — **Whole skill bypasses advertised guard**
  The guard claims "no bundled skill" carries forbidden residue, but `const EXEMPT = new Set(["migrate-pai-purpose"])` skips that skill before checking any pattern. The stated reason covers its Claude-home references, not its PAI-tree paths or identity placeholders, so the test cannot support the universal claim.

- **[important]** `src/skills/the-algorithm/references/algorithm.md:340` — **Audit references deleted enumeration**
  The mandatory audit says each name must appear in `"the closed enumeration"` and rejects `"anything outside the list"`, but this change removed that list in favor of the per-machine registry. Following this gate leaves no enumeration to check and can reject valid installed capabilities.
  Fix: Require names to appear in `algorithm capabilities --list`.

- **[important]** `src/algorithm-capabilities.ts:698` — **Contract minting is forgeable**
  The comment claims “Only the `Contract("…")` parser may mint one,” but `AlgorithmCapabilityDefinition.origin` is public and a caller can pass `origin: "soma-home"` with `kind: "contract"`, bypassing this guard. Downstream code is misled into treating an untrusted provenance label as proof that the parser produced the definition.

- **[blocker]** `src/cli/graph.ts:517` — **Preflight executes untrusted repo hooks**
  `"argv: [\"git\", \"-C\", dir, \"status\", \"--porcelain=v2\", \"--branch\"]"` runs before probe authorization. `git status` honors `core.fsmonitor`; tracker-supplied `cwd`/`repo` can point to a local attacker-controlled repository and execute its hook even when the registry later refuses the probe.
  Fix: Disable repository-controlled fsmonitor hooks for this status invocation and add a regression test.

- **[important]** `docs/work-graph.md:158` — **Pager threat claim is false**
  The claim that both overrides are needed because "git status would otherwise execute a program named by the target repo's own config" overstates the pager risk: the implementation explicitly states `core.pager` is "not reachable from --porcelain" in `src/cli/graph.ts:526`. This misdescribes the security boundary to readers relying on the documented hardening.

On the second half of your fix note — "an actual probe tree with no HEAD is bypassed": the pointer now names every tree and **withholds when any of them lacks a readable HEAD**, since `n/n passed` beside a pointer accounting for only some of the trees is the overstatement this PR exists to remove. That is a deliberate **tightening**: an `auto` node whose probe runs in a non-git directory no longer closes. No such node exists in this repo (every declared probe is a `command` in the checkout), and the alternative — anchoring on the trees that happen to have a HEAD — is the behaviour you flagged.

**Preflight executes untrusted repo hooks** *(blocker)* — accepted, and it is a hazard this PR introduced: before it, no git command ran in a tracker-named directory. The status call now carries `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.pager=cat`, and `probeTreeStatusArgv(dir)` is exported so the overrides are a checked property rather than a comment. Regression test asserts the exact argv.

**Absolute paths leak into tracker receipts** *(important)* — accepted, with the narrower fix. An opaque identifier would defeat the point, since the receipt exists so a reader can tell one checkout from another — and below `~` the path is exactly what does that.    ground-truth fact:

   - index-freshness (GATES health) — INDEX.md is at least as new as every
     durable note (an episodic write does NOT stale it; the INDEX is durable-only).
   - digest-coverage (info) — session/action note counts vs monthly digest files.
   - orphaned-archive (info) — archived episodic notes missing from a digest.
   - event-ratio (info) — event-stream lines over valid-note count.
   The CLI EXITS NON-ZERO (SomaCliError) when unhealthy — a schema-invalid note
   or a stale INDEX — so it can gate CI / a pre-consolidation check. The report
   is still printed. Symlinked dirs/files are never followed (only real entries
   are audited).

  fail after notes were already archived. The per-write assert (which struck after

It fetches one RSS 2.0 or Atom feed over `https:` (10 s limit for the whole
fetch; up to 5 redirects, every hop `https:`; body at most 2 MiB), counts the
items dated in the last `--window-days` days (RSS `<pubDate>`; Atom
`<published>`, else `<updated>`; items dated after now do not count), and
publishes one `execution.run.finished` with `ran.kind = job`, `ran.ref =
goal-sense/G<n>`, `serves.goal = G<n>` and `state {subject: G<n>, value}`. At
least `--min` items is `on-track`, fewer (including none) is `off-track`. An
item with a missing or unparseable date is skipped with one stderr warning
naming its position. A failed fetch (network, timeout, non-2xx, a redirect off
`https:` or past 5 hops, a body over 2 MiB) or a body with
neither an `<rss>` nor a `<feed>` root publishes `outcome: failed` with no
state, names the cause on stderr and exits 1. A goal id that is not `G<n>`, a
non-`https:` URL or a `--window-days`/`--min` that is not a positive integer
exits 2 before anything is fetched or published. The envelope carries the goal
id and the state only, never the URL, the feed title or item text. The feed is
scanned for its item blocks and date elements, not parsed as XML: links are
never followed and entities never resolved. stdout prints the value, the count
and the ledger result; with `SOMA_PRINCIPAL` unset nothing is published and the
exit code is 0 (1 on a failed fetch).

Delivery fails open. The emit (connect, replay the spool, publish, close)
gives up after 2 s. A failed or timed-out emit leaves the verb's output, exit

to the Soma event log. An envelope whose send failed stays in

it. A configuration failure (missing creds file, non-loopback URL without
creds) is refused before the spool and is not replayed. A timed-out emit is
abandoned, not cancelled: its bounded connect or publish can keep the process
alive a few seconds after the verb has printed.

Each transition has a gate. For example, THINK requires at least one recorded
current-state probe (an observation whose evidence kind is `probed` or `tested`,
not a `specified` spec-restatement), PLAN requires selected capabilities,
BUILD requires a criterion-mapped plan, VERIFY requires every plan step to be
done or blocked, LEARN requires every criterion to be passed, dropped, or
deferred-probe and refuses a `passed` criterion whose evidence kind is
explicitly `specified` (it must claim probed/tested, or be marked deferred-probe;
legacy criteria with no recorded evidence kind are grandfathered), and COMPLETE
rejects structured capability selections that were not invoked or removed. This is the part that adds determinism: the LLM can propose content,
but Soma decides whether the process is allowed to advance.

The harness is driven through explicit mutations rather than substrate-specific
conversation tricks. The portable command surface covers `new`, `list`, `show`,
`classify`, `capabilities`, `invoke`, `remove-capability`, `plan`, `observe`,
`decision`, `change`, `step`, `verify`, `learn`, `reflect`, `reflections`,
`advance`, and `resume`. `reflect` records a per-run meta-reflection (deterministic
gate-flags + the model's "a smarter run would have…" signals); `reflections --digest`
ranks the cross-run improvement backlog. `resume` accepts
an explicit `--until-phase` handoff boundary so a relay substrate can stop
before consuming downstream phases. `classify` is Soma's
UserPromptSubmit mode classifier: it chooses MINIMAL, NATIVE, or ALGORITHM and
maps Algorithm prompts to E1-E5 before a run is created. This adapts the useful
part of PAI's Algorithm tool while leaving Claude-only PRD parsing, prompt
curls, and loop execution outside the kernel.

no substrate-home environment override in its adapter; its default resolves
from HOME/USERPROFILE.

matches refuses the operation before any write. A retry attaches an authenticated

forge rather than a search index or local receipt, so a process restart keeps

a closing keyword before the node's number merges — observed live on #588, two
seconds after #590 merged, `commit_id: null`. The keyword was past-tense prose,
"my first attempt closed #588", which GitHub parses like any `Closes #N`; #600).
A close run from a dev
tree warns on stderr rather than refusing — refusing would make the primitive
undevelopable, and the warning keeps the gap visible state rather than silent.

commit — because "merged" and "enforced" are different dates (§1 clause 5 puts
enforcement in the install), and a receipt must say which rules produced it.

  /repos/{repo}/issues/{n}/parent` endpoint. The ordinary issue response carries
  no `parent` key, and treating it as authoritative would silently degrade
  conjunct 4 from "the graph root's author may ratify" into "a ticket's own
  author may ratify its close". Keeping this one-edge read out of GraphQL also
  removes a separate quota dependency from every `readNode`. When a subtree's
  normal GraphQL observation is rate-limited, the membership walk restarts
  wholly through paginated REST `/sub_issues` reads, preserving depth-first

  visited node plus blocker hydration. That fallback may blend observations
  across more calls; it is availability after quota exhaustion, not the normal

leak, not an egress or an attack. The finding carries a hint, and the decision
reason appends it, so the substrate tells the model the recovery:
`soma redact <path>` prints the file with secret values masked and keeps keys,
structure, paths and public NKEYs. It masks JWTs, NKEY seeds, creds and
private-key blocks, long hex, URL userinfo passwords, and the whole value of a
secret-named key: quoted values up to their closing quote, numbers included,
and YAML block scalars line by line. A whole `${VAR}` (or `${VAR}/path`) is a
reference and stays; a bare `$NAME` is one only in `.env`, where dotenv
expands it, so `password: $ecretPass` in yaml is masked. In `.env` it masks
every value that is not a path, a reference or a literal, and keeps numbers only under
keys that are not secret-named (`PORT=8080`). A value counts as a path only
when it uses path characters and has a second segment or an extension, so a
base64 secret that starts with `/` is still masked. The finding names the path, not its content, so the path lands in
the trace and the event metadata.
